shangul-mangul.title: Jingle, Jangle and Little Grape
shangul-mangul.tradition: Iranian folk tale «شنگول و منگول و حبه‌ی انگور» (oral tradition); the same tale type as the Brothers Grimm's "The Wolf and the Seven Young Kids" (Kinder- und Hausmärchen, no. 5, 1812).
shangul-mangul.source_note: Grimms' Fairy Tales, Project Gutenberg eBook #2591 (19th-century English translation): "The Wolf and the Seven Little Kids" — the rough voice, the black feet, the floured paws.
shangul-mangul.public_domain: Folk tale; the Grimm text and its 19th-century translation are in the public domain.
shangul-mangul.changes: Retold for this site: three kids as in the Persian tale, a secret song as the final check, and a gentle ending (nobody is eaten).

verified.by: Claude (text checked against the Gutenberg file)

shangul-mangul.note: An old Iranian folk tale, also told by the Brothers Grimm as "The Wolf and the Seven Young Kids". We retold it with a gentler ending.

fa.title: شنگول و منگول و حبه‌ی انگور
fa.note: قصه‌ای قدیمی و ایرانی که برادران گریم هم آن را با نامِ «گرگ و هفت بزغاله» نوشته‌اند. ما آن را با پایانی مهربان‌تر بازگو کرده‌ایم.

fox-and-grapes.title: The Fox and the Sweet Grapes
fox-and-grapes.tradition: Aesop's fable "The Fox and the Grapes"; in Persian the saying "دستم به انگور نمی‌رسد، می‌گویم ترش است" comes from the same idea.
fox-and-grapes.source_note: Aesop's Fables; a new translation by V. S. Vernon Jones, Project Gutenberg eBook #11339: "The Fox and the Grapes" — the hungry fox, the high vine, the jumping, and "I see now they are quite sour".
fox-and-grapes.public_domain: Ancient fable; the 1912 Vernon Jones translation is in the public domain.
fox-and-grapes.changes: Retold for this site: Little Grape the goat asks "What makes you say that?", and a ladder lets the fox taste the grapes (in Aesop's fable he simply walks away).

verified.by: Claude (text checked against the Gutenberg file)

fox-and-grapes.note: An ancient fable by Aesop. We added a clever goat and a ladder.

fa.title: روباه و انگورهای شیرین
fa.note: افسانه‌ای کهن از ازوپ. ما یک بزغالهٔ باهوش و یک نردبان به آن اضافه کرده‌ایم.
